A1.justification: Both PDFs describe POLYRATING, and their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison. v2 Appendices C–E match v3 Appendices D–F; v3 inserts a new Appendix C.

before.justification: v2 reports original bias estimates, sample-efficiency experiments and fitted leaderboards in Section 4, plus rating-system comparisons and detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a model-version evaluation experiment in Appendix C and a Glicko comparison in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a Gaussian prior coupling the base ratings of consecutive minor model versions and a corresponding loss penalty in Equation (4). This is a limited extension; the original linear rating model and optimization methods remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation of updated models when their earlier versions have already been evaluated, using Chatbot Arena data. Existing language, coding, hardness, decomposable-task, Wildbench and MixEval-Hard coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Appendix B and Figure 4 add Glicko as an evaluated comparator alongside Bradley–Terry, Davidson, Rao–Kupper and the accuracy-based system. Glicko was cited but not included in this comparison in v2.

E3.justification: The new Appendix C.2 experiment identifies 43 subsequent versions among 129 models, separates their games from other games, and varies training samples while evaluating held-out games. Other games are available to both compared systems. This adds a protocol without revising the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B extends its analysis of rating-system design choices to examine approximate Glicko fitting, beyond the previous comparison of Bradley–Terry, draw models and accuracy-based ratings. This adds evidence concerning the suitability of approximate rating updates.

E5.justification: Both versions retain bootstrap uncertainty reporting, including main-text 2-sigma intervals and appendix 95% pivotal intervals. v3 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed information, statistical tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 5 newly reports 38% sample-efficiency improvement at 10,000 samples for version evaluation. Figure 4 adds Glicko's poorer performance and changes existing loss curves. Section 4.3 revises leaderboard findings, although its new Chinese-gain counts of 67 and 97 disagree with the 47 and 94 positive entries displayed in unchanged Tables 7 and 8.

T1.justification: Appendix C introduces the consecutive-version pair set, a Gaussian rating-difference assumption and the regularized version objective. The existing convexity and convergence theorems, lemmas and proofs are substantively unchanged after moving from Appendix C to D.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about bias quantification, sample efficiency, cross-task comparability and optimality, including the 41% and 77% headline figures.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 replaces individual Yi/Llama examples with broader provider-level Chinese interpretations and an English training-history explanation. Appendix B newly discourages approximate rating systems, and Appendix C limits version coupling to minor updates. Section 6's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 replaces the supplementary-material code pointer with a repository address. Appendix E newly reports runs taking at most six hours on a single CPU, including million-sample settings. These are additional access instructions and computational disclosures.

R1.justification: v3 adds Abdi et al. (2021) on multivariate Glicko and Coulom (2008) on whole-history rating. It connects the version prior to Coulom and expands its positioning against AlpacaEval and approximate multivariate systems; most related work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the leaderboard discussion and related-work passages, explains the sample-efficiency measure, inserts the model-version appendix and relabels subsequent appendices. It also removes acknowledgements and adds conference headers. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 5, redraws Figure 4 with Glicko, changes its aspect ratio and tick spacing, and moves Figure 2 from page 6 to page 7 above Figure 3. Other changes involve headers, spacing and captions; the table organization is broadly retained.

improvement.justification: The specified model-version extension and supporting experiment add practical value, while the Glicko comparison, runtime disclosure and repository pointer improve evaluation breadth and reproducibility. These are limited gains: the main results and proofs remain unchanged, and the rewritten leaderboard discussion still conflicts with its tables, replacing v2's erroneous Yi-only claim with incorrect aggregate counts.
